sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface staining of heterologous cells confirmed comparable surface expression of Myc-tagged SALM5 and its deletion variants (L2); neurite outgrowth function not measured for the tagged construct specifically.
sites.rationale: Mouse SALM5 (LRFN5 ortholog) carries a Myc tag between its aa 19 and 20, which is the N-terminal region of the mature ectodomain just after signal-peptide cleavage. Human LRFN5 SP ends at residue 17 (A); the equivalent N-terminal tag position in human canonical numbering is insert_after_residue=17, placing the tag before Q18 (first mature residue). This avoids the dense cysteine cluster at C20/C24/C26 (LRRNT disulfides) that begins 3 residues downstream, and is 512 residues from the TM boundary. The mouse SP length is uncertain relative to human (17 aa), so the exact mouse-to-human residue mapping carries one-residue ambiguity; the N-terminal junction (after SP cleavage) is the most defensible human equivalent. Full-length mouse SALM5 (ortholog of human LRFN5) expressed in pGW1 with a Myc epitope tag inserted between aa 19 and 20 of the mouse sequence; L2 (same paper) confirms surface display of the tagged construct by surface staining in heterologous cells.

sources.claim: For Myc tagging of SALMs, the epitope was inserted between aa 16 and 17 of mouse SALM3 and aa 19 and 20 of mouse SALM5, respectively, in pGW1 (British Biotechnology).

literature_notes: L2 (PMC4881023) validates surface expression of the same Myc-tagged SALM5 construct described in L1 and does not introduce a new junction; it is used to set validation_level=surface_only for the L1 site. L3 (PMC2602877) reports epitope-tagged SALMs distributed in neurons but names no residue and provides no construct details; it does not pin a different junction and adds no new site. The human LRFN5 N-terminal region contains a tight cysteine cluster (C20, C24, C26, C37) forming LRRNT disulfides; inserting at positions 18 or 19 (closer to C20) was considered but rejected as it would place the tag 1–2 residues from a disulfide cysteine. No intracellular or function-abrogating positions were reported in the ledger.
